verdicts.where: The restless dead who cannot lie until given the rite they were denied: unburied Elpenor in the Odyssey and Palinurus in the Aeneid, the Witcher 3 botchling that is laid only by a name and a burial, the Dead of Garth Nix's Sabriel who keep returning until a bell sends them on; Supernatural's salt-and-burn, without which the ghost comes back; trolls that regenerate unless burned. Three rites each answered by one kind of harm, read off the body, with the failure arriving on the bell, belongs to none of them.

Pwyll in the Mabinogion, who must strike Hafgan exactly once because a second blow would restore him (the blow-count rules of folk tale); the cat's nine lives; Smaug and Achilles, whom only the right blow gets through; hit-count bosses and flat damage thresholds in games. The knell's 3, 6 and 9 reused as a blow count, and the stand-near term, come from no story.

Kill the leader and the host stops: the Keystone Army of Ender's Game, the droid army switching off in The Phantom Menace; elephants standing over their dead in nature films; daze and pacify effects that break on damage. Graded, timed mourning that punishes the player for interrupting it is its own.

'If thy right hand offend thee, cut it off', where only the part that offended pays; the medieval trials of animals and objects behind the film The Hour of the Pig; charm and disarm effects in games. Choosing between the two by whether the attacker was moving is in no story I know.

Blinded Polyphemus groping after Odysseus; A Quiet Place, where any sound gives you away; Mr Magoo walking straight through trouble; Cadmus' stone that sets the dragon's-teeth warriors on each other; coins on the eyes as Charon's fare. A blindness that fixes the heading and is broken by the player's own noise is its own.

The King of the Wood at Nemi in Frazer's The Golden Bough, 'the priest who slew the slayer, and shall himself be slain': whoever kills the marked one becomes the marked one. Halo's Juggernaut game type runs exactly that chain, everyone hunting whoever holds the mark. Cadmus' stone among the dragon's-teeth men and Shirley Jackson's The Lottery supply the crowd turning on one of its own; tag supplies 'you're it'.
verdicts.mutation: Hand the cry on by hearing, not by the kill: when a felon falls, the cry passes to the pursuer standing farthest from the player, so the chase always rolls outward through the crowd and away, and the player steers it by where they stand instead of the killer inheriting the mark.

verdicts.where: 'Stay on the path' in Little Red Riding Hood and 'stick to the road' in An American Werewolf in London; routed units walking off the map edge in Total War; banishment effects. Spoiling a protected walk on purpose to turn it into a triple-value kill is its own.

Christian's burden of sin on his back in The Pilgrim's Progress, shed only at the cross; the sin-eater who takes a corpse's sins on himself (Francine Rivers' The Last Sin Eater, Atwood's 'The Sin Eater'); the demon of Fallen (1998) that jumps to the nearest body when its host dies; Marley's chain. A visible load of harm bought with speed, passed between the dead and the player, is none of these.

Say the name three times and it comes for you: Beetlejuice, Bloody Mary in the mirror, Candyman. The Taboo on Voldemort's name in Deathly Hallows, where speaking it lets his followers find the speaker anywhere, is the case of a dead Crier naming the player; true names that give a hold across any distance (Earthsea, Rumpelstiltskin) and the two-way link between Harry and Voldemort give the symmetry.
verdicts.mutation: Bind the hold to a posted bill rather than a thrice-spoken name: the crier nails a proclamation to the nearest door, range and walls stop counting between crier and named only while both are within sight of that bill, and the named thing goes to tear it down rather than run at the crier, so the bond becomes a fight over a place on the map.

verdicts.where: Procrustes' bed and Cinderella's slipper, which serve only the one they fit, and Goldilocks' 'just right'; measures taken from the body, the cubit and the foot; attribute requirements on gear in role-playing games. Attributes as the units the skill text is written in come from no story.

The Very Deep Pit that Pooh and Piglet dig for a Heffalump, tiger pits, the spiked pits of zombie fiction; Hamlet's gravedigger and the sexton as stock churchyard furniture; trap-laying classes. Standing still to dig, and leading the crowd across a hole that fills and closes, is its own.

Moses lifting his rod to part the sea (The Ten Commandments), the walls closing on whoever is caught inside; the lictors and mace-bearers who cleared a road; the flying wedge. As a class's ordinary walk that covers only the front, it is its own.

Townsfolk pelting attackers from upper windows: Quasimodo pouring molten lead from Notre-Dame, the 'gardyloo' of old Edinburgh, the French castle flinging a cow in Monty Python and the Holy Grail; shrines and turrets switched on by passing in games. The knocker-up's round as a route of turrets is in no story.

Charon, who carries the dead across for the coin they hold (Aeneid VI, Percy Jackson), and Spiritfarer, where the player takes over his job and ferries spirits to their rest; Grim Fandango's Manny selling the dead their passage. The passenger who climbs onto your back and weighs you down is St Christopher's child and Sinbad's Old Man of the Sea.
verdicts.mutation: Reckon fares like a Thames waterman's rather than Charon's: each waiting dead names a landing by the number on its token and pays one coin and one kill's experience per stair passed on the way, so the Ferryman chooses short hops or long crossings over a map of numbered stairs instead of shuttling the dead to rest between two fixed banks.

verdicts.where: The swinging blade of Poe's 'The Pit and the Pendulum', the tilting quintain, the sweeper arm of Wipeout; the troll who takes toll at the bridge in The Three Billy Goats Gruff; tethered beams in arcade shooters. A bar from a planted post to the keeper, charging double on repeat passes, is its own.

The burning glass every child has turned on ants, Archimedes' mirrors against the Roman fleet, the Staff of Ra in Raiders of the Lost Ark throwing a spot of sunlight on the map-room floor; vampires burned by light through a window. Harm placed by the district's one light, on the far side of the bearer, is its own.
The self-winding watch, wound by its wearer's walking; Aeolus' bag of winds let out all at once; charge-by-moving items and stand-to-fire characters in games. No story has it as a rule.

The fortified village of Seven Samurai that lets the bandits in only where the samurai want them; buffalo-jump drive lanes; tower-defence mazing. Walls that are the spoil of the class's own graves and vanish when the graves fill are its own.

The sin-eater of Welsh border folklore, retold in Francine Rivers' The Last Sin Eater, the film The Order (2003) and Atwood's 'The Sin Eater': eating over the corpse lets it rest and the eater carries the sin. Geist: The Sin-Eaters makes the name a player role; corpse-consuming stacks exist in Diablo and Path of Exile. Growing stronger and slower without limit until the vigil has to end is in none of them.

The Pied Piper of Hamelin, a column that falls in behind its leader, follows helplessly and is led to its end in the Weser; Death leading the dancers in a line over the hill at the close of The Seventh Seal; the danse macabre. The rule that turning back breaks it is Orpheus and Lot's wife.
verdicts.mutation: Have the parted dead stand rather than follow: they fall into two still files facing inward along the route the Verger has just walked, unable to strike for 5 s, and both files strike inward at once if the Verger turns back into the lane, so the crowd becomes a corridor laid behind the player to aim along, not a train led like the Piper's rats.

verdicts.where: Sleeping Beauty's castle, everyone asleep where they stood until the spell ends; 'the curfew tolls the knell of parting day' in Gray's Elegy; sleep effects that break on damage. Sleepers that cannot be touched and wake on the district bell are its own.

A Quiet Place, where the creatures hunt only by sound and the family draws them off with fireworks; the thumpers of Dune that call the worm away from whoever walks without rhythm; the noise-led hordes of World War Z and The Walking Dead; Tremors. A whole horde that loses the silent one and goes to the loudest thing is that premise.
verdicts.mutation: Let the dead gather to a house of mourning instead of to noise: each door the Mute stands at for 1 s is draped, and every dead thing beyond 6 m walks to the nearest draped door and waits there for the body to be brought out, so the class places the horde by marking houses of death, woken or not, rather than by luring it with sound.

verdicts.where: Gaffer Hexam and Rogue Riderhood fishing drowned bodies out of the Thames for what they bring in Dickens' Our Mutual Friend; the bounty hunter hauling in a corpse (For a Few Dollars More, The Mandalorian); the carried bodies of Death Stranding. The cheap near bank against the dear far bank is its own.

Undertale, where a spared monster pays gold and no experience; weakening without fainting in order to catch, in Pokemon; spared foes who repay, from The Lion and the Mouse to the grateful dead of folk tale. Tuning the bar weak so that the crowd survives three payings is its own.

The weekly Bills of Mortality in Defoe's A Journal of the Plague Year; the Hydra, where every one cut down is made up by more; banishing an enemy type from the pool in games. Banishment chosen by what is laid most, renewed at every toll, is in no story.

Sunlight passed from mirror to mirror down a tomb in adventure films, the Staff of Ra in Raiders of the Lost Ark, the light-bending puzzles of Zelda and Tomb Raider; placed turrets. Panels whose patch is fixed by the map's one light and thrown on through one another are their own.

Hot potato and musical chairs, where whoever holds it when the music stops takes it all; Pepys' candle auctions; stored-damage skills released on one target. A pot filled by fighting a crowd and dropped on the last one struck is its own.

The weighing of the heart against Maat's feather in the Book of the Dead, Zeus' golden scales sinking Hector's fate in Iliad XXII, 'weighed in the balances and found wanting' (Daniel 5); Pain Split in Pokemon, which evens two health bars. Automatic, nearest pair only, and herded by the player, it is its own.

Corpse roads and spirit paths of folklore, the belief that spirits can travel only in straight lines (hence the zig-zag bridges of Chinese gardens), Irish fairy paths; the Roman soldiers seen marching their old road through the cellar of York's Treasurer's House; conveyor lanes in tower defence. A road drawn between the player's last two stops is its own.

The ghost that re-enacts its death at the same spot on its anniversary, the residual haunting of Nigel Kneale's The Stone Tape; Corpse Explosion in Diablo II, scaled by the corpse's full life; delayed blasts. Coming due at the death spot on a fixed half-minute, as a lap time, is its own.

Buffy the Vampire Slayer's cemetery patrol, waiting at a fresh grave to stake the fledgling as it claws out weak and dazed; Van Helsing in Lucy's tomb and the daylight round of the resting places in Dracula and 'Salem's Lot, dispatching the dead before they rise at full strength; calling the next wave early in tower defence.
verdicts.mutation: Make the rap a booking, not an early kill: a rapped mound's occupant rises at full life exactly 20 s later instead of at the toll, and pays double experience only if the player is within 8 m to see it up, as the knocker-up waited for the sleeper at the glass, so the quiet seconds are spent drawing up a timetable of risings and keeping it.

verdicts.where: The broken token of ballad and romance, lovers' halves of a ring or coin that prove each other when fitted, and the Greek symbolon; mark-and-detonate skills in games. Collecting by brushing past the marked body is its own.

Dorothy L. Sayers' The Nine Tailors, built on the tellers of the knell ('nine tailors make a man') and ending with a man killed by the bells; Donne's 'for whom the bell tolls'; overkill that carries on to the next target in games. A burst whose length is read off the victim's size is its own.

The belief Frazer records in The Golden Bough that to strike, stab or tread on a man's shadow wounds the man; Peter Pan's shadow, caught and sewn back on; Shikamaru's shadow techniques in Naruto; kage-fumi, shadow tag. A real lamp-cast shadow used as an extended body for the player's skills is its own.

Lafcadio Hearn's 'The Soul of the Great Bell': the casting fails until the founder's daughter leaps into the metal, and then the bell rings; the Emille Bell legend of a child poured into King Seongdeok's bell; the bell cast in a pit in Tarkovsky's Andrei Rublev, where everything hangs on whether it rings or cracks; builder's-sacrifice legends such as Master Manole. A bell that rings only with enough of the dead poured in is that story.
verdicts.mutation: Make the crack a matter of tempo, not of how many die: metal that stops flowing sets in a cold shut, so the bell rings only if bodies keep falling within 5 m with no gap over 1.5 s from first to last, and the ring grows with the length of the unbroken pour, so the player must keep the killing steady rather than merely plentiful.

verdicts.where: Hallowed ground the dead cannot rise from: the Everlasting Rest of the Dungeons & Dragons Hallow spell, the holy ground of vampire fiction and Highlander; church floors paved with ledger stones; slowing ground effects. Territory laid down by where the kills fall is its own.
The chessboard of Through the Looking-Glass and the two halves of the yin-yang; buff and debuff zones in games. One lozenge whose halves bind both sides, aligned by the player's heading, is its own.

The sheep set on the right hand and the goats on the left in Matthew 25, the sinister left of superstition; flank and backstab bonuses in games. A bonus by the player's own right and left is nothing I can place.

Burial with the feet to the east so that the dead rise facing the Second Coming, with priests laid the other way, as folk custom; the fixed wind that helps or hinders every shot in Worms; facing-based backstab bonuses. Harm by the map's compass is in no story.

Mass Effect's prime-and-detonate combos, where one power sets a state and a different power sets it off for extra harm; elemental combos in Divinity: Original Sin; the split token of romance. Holding back half of the first skill's own harm is its own detail.
'Don't fire until you see the whites of their eyes' at Bunker Hill; the bier waiting under the lychgate; charge-up supports in games. A skill that waits for a crowd by a visible count is its own.

The troll in The Three Billy Goats Gruff, letting the first goat over to wait for the bigger one behind; the Passover, the destroyer passing over the marked door to strike the next; piercing shots in games. Skipping the nearest to strike the next one harder is its own.
The narrowing black border of Victorian mourning paper itself; ramp-and-reset buffs in action games. Nothing in stories that I can place.

Crossing the streams in Ghostbusters, two beams that do something far greater where they meet; the locked wand-beams of Priori Incantatem in Goblet of Fire; tipper sweet spots in fighting games. One cast split into halves that meet at a single range is its own.

Grimm's Godfather Death, where every life is a candle burning down in Death's cave; Meleager's log; the enchanted rose of Beauty and the Beast shedding petals as a clock; 'out, out, brief candle'. A reserve pool that is also the run's clock is its own.

Aladdin's cave, 'touch nothing but the lamp', and the fairy-mound rule that whoever takes nothing comes out safe; Scarlett O'Hara in full black, forbidden to dance, in Gone with the Wind; stealth that shortens enemy sight. Grades that lighten on the bell are its own.

Whittier's poem 'Telling the Bees' and the custom it records; the household brownie and Melusine, helpers who leave the moment a duty or taboo is broken; pickup-magnet pets in games. A magnet whose price is a second's stillness after each big death is its own.
The deodand itself and the medieval prosecution of animals and objects (The Hour of the Pig); thorns and reflect effects. Seizing the attacker and paying out its appraised value is its own.

Walking through the dead smeared in their guts in The Walking Dead's 'Guts', pretending to be zombies to cross the crowd in Shaun of the Dead; Tom Sawyer at his own funeral; wave-skip and invisibility pickups. The rule that nothing is skipped and all of it rises on the bell is its own.

The gift that must not be opened, Pandora's jar and Urashima Taro's box; funeral biscuits kept for years; banked rerolls and saved level-ups. Three different ends, by whether it is opened, carried out or left behind by the dead, are its own.

Charon's fare paid in advance ('Don't pay the ferryman until he gets you to the other side'); extraction beacons bought in extraction shooters. A rising standing fare for exits, taken from the purse the exits protect, is its own.

Cinderella's finery that lasts only until the clock strikes twelve, so she must leave the ball in time; the Little Mermaid's three days; Faust's term; timed power-ups. A doubled pick kept only by leaving, where overstaying also costs the pick before it, is its own.
Tula bhara, a ruler weighed against gold; the weigh-in before a prizefight; Money = Power in The Binding of Isaac, harm per coin held. Measured once, at a known toll, it is its own.

Maupassant's 'The Necklace', borrowed finery whose loss costs ten years; fairy loans that must go back by a set day; temporary shields. A return errand across the map, paid in future picks if missed, is its own.

The Green Lantern ring that seeks a successor when its dying bearer falls, the Slayer line of Buffy, heirloom swords such as Narsil; heirs and heirlooms in Rogue Legacy and Darkest Dungeon. Insuring one built skill, with a refund if it is never needed, is its own.

The clickers of The Last of Us, blind and hunting by sound; Amando de Ossorio's Blind Dead, eyeless revenants who find their victims by ear; A Quiet Place; Mr Magoo walking straight into things. The ruler-straight walker that re-aims at the last cast after every bump is its own.

The Gentlemen of Buffy's 'Hush', who take every voice in town; the Silence spell that stops casting in Dungeons & Dragons and Final Fantasy, the beholder's anti-magic cone; Oliver Twist hired out as a funeral mute by Sowerberry the undertaker. A harmless door-keeper undone by a jostle is its own.

The close of Dracula: the gypsies carry the Count's box toward his castle against the sunset, and the hunters must cut down the bearers and deal with him while he lies helpless in it before he can rise; also caravan and escort interceptions in games. A sleeping undead carried to the place where it will wake in power is that chase.
verdicts.mutation: Turn the stakes from the rising to the road: wherever the bearers fall and the bier touches ground off a resting stone, that spot becomes a new stone and the corpse road bends through it for the rest of the vigil, after the belief that carrying a corpse across land makes it a right of way, so where the player drops the bier redraws the path the dead walk.

verdicts.where: Devil's Snare in Harry Potter, which grips harder the more you struggle; the Chinese finger trap; the Weeping Angels, held still by the player's own attention; the mortsafes of Burke-and-Hare churchyards; shielded enemies. A cage renewed by every blow, which self-casting skills keep feeding, is its own.

The pod-person's point-and-shriek at the end of Invasion of the Body Snatchers (1978), which sets the whole town on the one marked; the Eye of Sauron; Aboriginal bone-pointing; Defoe's searchers of the dead; sniper aiming lines. A spotter whose line the horde itself breaks is its own.

The will-o'-the-wisp, a light always just ahead that leads travellers into the mire; the link-boy who led his customer to waiting robbers, as London lore has it; buff-carrying support enemies. A light placed by the player's own heading is its own.

The beggar at the door who must be given to, from the disguised enchantress turned away in Beauty and the Beast to Perrault's 'Diamonds and Toads' and Baucis and Philemon; thief enemies that grab pickups and run. Dole taken in exchange for ward-strokes is its own.

Wanyudo and Katawaguruma, the burning cart-wheels of Japanese folklore that roll the roads taking whoever they meet; the rolling boulder of Raiders of the Lost Ark; Christine, the object that kills; indestructible bouncing hazards in arcade games. Changing owner when it strikes the player is its own.

Burke and Hare, Jerry Cruncher the 'resurrection man' of A Tale of Two Cities, Stevenson's 'The Body Snatcher' and its 1945 film; Diablo III's treasure goblins and other loot thieves. Thieves who also carry off bodies that would stand again, and so are sometimes welcome, are their own.
The Roman testudo of Asterix and the phalanx; the gashadokuro, a giant made of the unburied dead; Defoe's great pit at Aldgate. In a horde game, one rigid slab to be out-turned is its own.

'Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein' (Proverbs 26:27), Haman hanged on his own gallows, 'hoist with his own petard'; the strokes of age in The Nine Tailors; ring-with-a-gap patterns in bullet-hell bosses. A barrage as long as the player's level is its own.

Ali's rope-a-dope, letting the other man punch himself out; Bilbo carrying a cup off Smaug's hoard; Zeninage (Gil Toss) in Final Fantasy, attacks paid for in money; bosses that tire. A boss whose life is a purse it spends by attacking is its own.

The ghosts of Richard III's victims rising before Bosworth to say 'despair and die'; Defoe's shut-up plague houses; Disable in Pokemon, sealing a move; arena lock-ins. A replay of the player's own kill count is its own.

Tenebrae itself; the figures vanishing one by one in And Then There Were None; the torch of Darkest Dungeon; shrinking-arena and safe-spot boss phases. The countdown carried in the room's real candles is its own.

The Santa Compana of Galicia, a procession of the dead walking the parish paths; Welsh corpse candles and phantom funerals that walk the route a coffin will take; the Night Parade of One Hundred Demons; the herd led down a walled road in The Walking Dead; lane maps in tower defence. A horde fought from the banks of its own road is its own.

'Bring out your dead!' and the plague cart of Monty Python and the Holy Grail; Defoe's houses shut up under a red cross; the marked doors of the Passover; spawner doors in arcade games. Doors whose timers can be put off at a price are their own.

Quasimodo's 'Sanctuary!' in The Hunchback of Notre Dame, the holy ground of Highlander and vampire fiction; the Beverley frith stool and its crosses; safe zones in games. Graded rings rationed in seconds are their own.

The Floating Market of Gaiman's Neverwhere, open only at its set times; Rossetti's 'Goblin Market'; Brigadoon; the cabbage merchant whose stall is wrecked in every chase in Avatar: The Last Airbender; mid-run shops. Stalls open only in the dangerous seconds after each bell are their own.
Dots and Boxes, territory in Go, completed cities in Carcassonne; the beating of the bounds itself. Nothing in stories; as the whole shape of a passive tree it is its own.

The troll who takes toll at the bridge in The Three Billy Goats Gruff, the Bridge of Death and 'none shall pass' in Monty Python and the Holy Grail; travel nodes in passive trees. A crossing charge that lapses at a printed level is its own.
The ossuaries of Sedlec and Hallstatt; summon caps where the oldest minion is replaced; diminishing returns. Nothing in stories.

The bloodstains and messages Dark Souls leaves where others died, the trails worn by many players' footsteps in Death Stranding, pilgrim steps worn hollow; meta-currency unlocks. A discount laid down by where the player's own dead spent their points is its own.

The urSkeks of The Dark Crystal, split into Skeksis and Mystics far apart and whole again only when rejoined; the split medallion that proves a lost heir; the Triforce; set bonuses. Pairs hidden in the tree by notch pattern are their own.

Jarndyce and Jarndyce in Bleak House, where contesting a will eats the estate; the conditional inheritance of Brewster's Millions; Mjolnir's inscription, power only 'if he be worthy'; conditional affixes and class items. Every property with its own heir is its own.
The Exchequer tally and the broken token of romance; fusing duplicate items in games. Matching by notch pattern, with a hard limit on rework, is its own.

Elric's Stormbringer drinking the souls of the slain, Sigurd tasting Fafnir's heart; Mega Man taking a weapon from each boss he beats; weapons that earn traits from kills. The order of first kills deciding which pool each property comes from is its own.
Unidentified items and gear that levels with use in role-playing games; Victorian mourning grades. Nothing in stories.

Cruentation as a story device: Siegfried's wounds bleed afresh when Hagen comes to the bier in the Nibelungenlied, dead Henry's bleed at Richard's approach in Richard III, and Scott's The Fair Maid of Perth turns on an ordeal of bier-right in which the suspects of a murder are summoned to pass the corpse. Leading the suspects past the bier to find the guilty one is that ordeal.
verdicts.mutation: Let the bier read degrees rather than name one culprit: each suspect carries a hidden share of the guilt, the bier runs redder the larger the share of whoever passes, and the reward depends on laying them in order of guilt, so the player compares three readings taken under pressure instead of sorting one murderer from two innocents.

verdicts.where: Quasimodo crying 'Sanctuary!' from Notre-Dame while the mob waits below; the chalk circle the dead cannot cross in Gogol's Viy and the protective circle held all night in The Devil Rides Out, with the things gathering outside it; the farmhouse ringed by the dead in Night of the Living Dead. Safety on a clock while the horde masses round, then breaking out, is that stock scene.
verdicts.mutation: Do not ring the character: the dead that arrive during the term go to keep watch on the district's gates instead, a watch building at each gate in turn, so the character steps out into a clear street with every exit watched and must choose which watch to break, rather than cutting out of a ring like a besieged magic circle.

verdicts.where: Musical chairs and king of the hill; the candle auction; NetHack's monsters picking up and wielding what they find. A prize that, when lost, walks off on an elite wearing it is its own.

Aladdin's 'One Jump Ahead', the thief chased by the whole market; Ealing's Hue and Cry (1947); the runner who draws the dead off the others in zombie films; loot-carrier events. A race against the horde for the same quarry is its own.

The beacons of Gondor lit across the hills; warding stones and the beating of the bounds; light-every-brazier puzzles in games. A ring along the spawning edge that pays in full only while whole is its own.

The past Avatars whose strength the living one draws on in Avatar: The Last Airbender; Inscryption's death cards, made from a dead run's cards and dealt into later runs; Rogue Legacy's family tree. A floor of the player's dead, laid by hand and valued by its neighbours, is its own.

Inigo Montoya, who spends his life training against the six-fingered man who killed his father in The Princess Bride; Ahab's whale; trophies hung in the hall (Gaston's antlers); the nemesis system of Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor. A bonus sized by what was lost, once per kind, is its own.
Victorian household mourning, as in Scarlett O'Hara's scandal at dancing in black in Gone with the Wind; rested-experience bonuses. A bonus set off by a death and barred from coin is its own.
The tellers and the strokes of age in Sayers' The Nine Tailors; Donne's bell; end-of-run tallies. Paying in strokes, with a fixed premium for dying, is its own.

Shylock's bond, falling due on a fixed day and paid in flesh; Dorian Gray, whose harm is held off and arrives all at once; the Brewmaster's Stagger in World of Warcraft and the rally of Bloodborne. One district bell that collects everything is its own.

Orpheus leading Eurydice out of death, saved only if he never looks back, and Lot's wife; 'stick to the road' in An American Werewolf in London; last-stand and second-wind rules. A life bought with a district closed for good is its own.
The safe havens of Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?, double or nothing; partial extraction. A doubling paid only on finishing alive is its own.

The vigil over the dead in Gogol's Viy, three nights of reading over the witch's body; Finnegan's Wake; ghost runs against a past self; heirs in Rogue Legacy. A short mode held as a wake to complete a dead character is its own.

'One if by land, and two if by sea' in Longfellow's 'Paul Revere's Ride'; the tellers of the knell and the bell-ringing cipher of The Nine Tailors; bells rung backwards as an alarm; wave previews. The forecast carried only in a count of strokes is its own.
